title: Modularization with Swift packages
summary: Split a big app into modules (feature, domain, core) with one-way dependencies. You get faster builds, clear ownership, enforced boundaries and faster tests and previews.
body: **In simple words:** Instead of one giant app target, you create packages: `Networking`, `DesignSystem`, `Profile`, `Feed`... Each compiles separately, and the compiler stops one feature from reaching into another's internals.
**Typical layers:** App shell → Feature modules (UI) → Feature interface modules → Domain/Services → Core (networking, persistence, design system, utilities). Arrows only point down.

**Interface / implementation split:** `ProfileInterface` (tiny: protocols, route types) and `Profile` (heavy implementation). Other features depend only on the interface, so changing Profile's code does not rebuild them, and there are no cycles.
**Benefits:** incremental builds, parallel builds, demo apps per feature for fast iteration, isolated tests, CODEOWNERS per module, `internal` really means internal.
**Pitfalls:** too many tiny modules (link and indexing overhead), a "Common" module that becomes a dumping ground, resources (`Bundle.module`), static library duplicates.
**Staff angle:** measure clean/incremental build and CI time before and after, extract core modules first, enforce dependency rules in CI, provide a module template generator.
keyPoints: Layered, one-way dependency graph; features never depend on other features' implementations.
Interface modules break cycles and reduce rebuilds.
Per-feature demo apps and tests speed iteration.
Use `package` access and `internal import` to avoid leaking dependencies.
Measure build times to prove the value.

code.caption: Feature with an interface split
code.text:
// Package.swift (excerpt)
.target(name: "ProfileInterface", dependencies: ["Core"]),
.target(name: "Profile", dependencies: ["ProfileInterface", "DesignSystem", "Networking"]),
.target(name: "Feed", dependencies: ["FeedInterface", "ProfileInterface"]),   // not "Profile"
.testTarget(name: "ProfileTests", dependencies: ["Profile"])

mistakes: Splitting into modules without an agreed dependency direction (cycles).
Putting everything shared into one "Common" module.
followups: **How do two features navigate to each other without depending on each other?** Through route types in interface modules and a router/registry resolved at the app level.
**SPM vs CocoaPods?** SPM is built into Xcode and the standard now; CocoaPods is in maintenance mode.
